paragraphs: The 520d has been a mainstay of the 5 Series diesel range since the F10 generation, spanning three generations under one badge. Early cars (F10/F11, 2010–2017) use the N47 — a 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel that's been well-documented for timing chain stretch at higher mileages. From 2017, the G30/G31-generation 520d switched to the B47, a newer engine with no equivalent pattern documented. The current G60 generation continues with the B47. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components, the known wear pattern, and even the rebuild specifics differ — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The 520d is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel fitted to the 520d from 2010 to 2017. Known for timing chain stretch over time — see the callout above. We replace the timing chain, guides, tensioners and gaskets as standard on every N47 rebuild.

The current 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel, fitted from 2017 onwards across the G30/G31 and G60 generations. A genuinely different design from the N47, generally reliable with no widely-documented timing chain pattern equivalent to its predecessor.

compatibility.intro: Because BMW 5 Series 520d can use the N47 or B47 engine code, fitting the wrong replacement risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N47 or B47) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 520d quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
